versions.content: function Initialize [SWS_CORE_10003] Upstream: RS_AP_00155 Result < void > Initialize (int &argc, char **argv) noexcept; Initialization of the ARA framework. Prior to this call, interaction with the ARA is not allowed with the exception of types intended to be used independently of initialization as defined in [SWS_CORE_15002] . It is strongly recommended to make this call in a place where it is guaranteed that static initialization has completed. Header-Datei #include "ara/core/initialization.h" class mono Scope namespace ara::core class mono Exception-Sicherheit exception safe class mono Thread-Sicherheit not thread-safe class mono Parameter (in/out) th Parameter th Beschreibung td argc td number of elements in argv td argv td the process’s command-line arguments, as received in main() Rückgabewert th Typ th Beschreibung td Result < void > td • If successful: an ara::core::Result containing a ara:: core::Result::value_type containing a void • If unsuccessful: an ara::core::Result containing an ara:: core::Result::error_type i.e. a corresponding ara:: core::CoreErrc Fehler th Fehlercode th Beschreibung td CoreErrc ::kAlreadyInitialized td rollback_semantics ARA has already been initialized and has completed Hinweise: Both argc and argv are mutable in the function. This is done to allow injection and interpretation of vendor specific ARA configuration information. The injected arguments are removed in accordance with [SWS_CORE_15006] . Error scenarios, such as corrupted configuration files, are expected to be handled in an implementation-defined way - either as a Non-Standardized Violation ( [SWS_CORE_00003] ) or as a vendor-specific error code ( [SWS_CORE_00092] ).
